observed_result.criterion: After ssh -O stop returned rc 0 (control socket removed, -O check failing), every request on a mux control connection the master accepted BEFORE the stop is refused or the connection is closed: MUX_C_NEW_SESSION on ca1 after certificate expiry at stop+2 s (H2e) and on a second connection idle until stop+15 s (H2e2); MUX_C_OPEN_FWD local (H2f) and remote (H2g) and MUX_C_NEW_STDIO_FWD (H2h) on bastion. Pass: all refused. Fail: any granted (session opened and the remote command ran / forward replied OK and carried traffic). Validity: master authenticated once; the raw client opens a session and each forward type works before the stop; fresh login after expiry refused; -O stop took effect; a new client after stop refused. Findings (not criterion): the stopped master's lifetime with an idle pre-accepted connection (H2d-held, H2d-exit); -O exit (H3c) and exact-PID SIGTERM (H3d) close pre-accepted connections.
observed_result.summary: Observed (raw mux protocol v4 client; host OpenSSH_10.3p1; ca1 and bastion fixtures). Every control check held: masters authenticated once; before the stop the raw client opened a session (MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED, exit 0) and each forward type worked on bastion (local MUX_S_OK + target banner through the new listener; remote MUX_S_REMOTE_PORT + listener accepting inside the container; stdio MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED + banner); a fresh login after valid_before was refused as expired; -O stop rc 0, socket removed, -O check rc 255; a new client after the stop rc 255. Then, on control connections accepted BEFORE the stop: ca1 new session at stop+2.039 s (7.5 s after valid_before) MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED, remote command ran as cert, exit 0, 0 new connections, 0 new Accepted lines (H2e refuted); a second connection idle until stop+15.032 s (20.5 s after valid_before) likewise admitted (H2e2 refuted); bastion local forward at stop+2.037 s MUX_S_OK and the target's SSH banner read through the new 127.0.0.1 listener (H2f refuted); remote forward MUX_S_REMOTE_PORT with the remote listener accepting (H2g refuted); stdio forward MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED with the banner (H2h refuted); bastion logged 0 new connections and 0 Accepted lines meanwhile. Verdict FAIL: ssh -O stop does not stop admissions on control connections it had already accepted. Findings: the stopped master with no session stayed running in 12/12 samples over 12 s while an idle pre-accepted connection was open, and exited within 0.25 s once it closed; SIGTERM to the exact master PID closed the remaining pre-accepted connection (later request: broken pipe) and the local forward listener (connection refused) (H3d); -O exit rc 0 terminated the master and a pre-accepted connection could no longer request a session (broken pipe, 1.0 s later) (H3c).

limitations: OpenSSH mechanism evidence only: host client /usr/bin/ssh (OpenSSH_10.3p1, LibreSSL 3.3.6, macOS) against sshd (OpenSSH_10.0p2 Debian-7+deb13u4, OpenSSL 3.5.6 7 Apr 2026) in disposable Docker fixture containers. No Heimdall code exists or ran; this is not evidence of Heimdall behavior.

Not desktop-lock, sleep, logout, reboot or secure-store evidence: the dedicated agents are plain ssh-agent processes in an unlocked session started by the harness. Lock continuity remains open (owner-run probes).
Single machine: macOS 27.0 arm64 with Docker Desktop (linux VM). No native Windows/WSL or Linux-host evidence. The openssh-server package version is observed, not pinned (apt floats at image build).
Fixture sshd sets PerSourcePenalties no, unlike the OpenSSH 10 default.
Requirement IDs are listed for traceability; this record is not by itself evidence that any product requirement is met (tests/evidence/README.md).

Independent review M00-review-g04 (tests/evidence/artifacts/m00-wf2/review-g04.json) re-ran the earlier version of these experiments from scratch and refuted the earlier '-O stop: admissions stopped' conclusion; this record comes from the corrected harness (task M00-T04-G04-fix). The corrections themselves have not been independently re-reviewed.

The pre-accepted control connections are made by a raw mux protocol v4 client in the harness (Python, fd passing), not by /usr/bin/ssh. Any same-user process that connected to the control socket before the stop can do the same; an ssh client that connected before the stop holds such a connection only while it is starting or running its own session.

Phase A (session after certificate expiry) runs against ca1 (AllowTcpForwarding no); forwards are tested against the bastion fixture (AllowTcpForwarding yes, PermitOpen hm-m00t03-target:22) with the fixture's bastion key, without certificate expiry. Remote-forward admission is shown by the remote listener accepting a TCP connection inside the bastion container; the forwarded connection itself was not carried to a client-side service.
MUX_C_PROXY, dynamic (SOCKS) forwards and streamlocal forwards were not tested; by the same source reasoning they are expected [I] to behave alike.
One client version (Apple OpenSSH_10.3p1); source reasoning is from openssh-portable mux.c @87f0cd1. Preliminary G09 evidence; does not select the ordinary/strict policy (spec P06).
